summary.intent: Execute Phase 34 (E2E Test Expansion & Staging Baselines) including account cleanup helpers, media/streaming tests, batch download tests, and staging performance baselines with BYO-IPFS load testing.
summary.outcome: All 4 plans completed with 13/13 must-haves verified. Real 200-client sustained load baselines captured (0.17% error rate, 11,174 ops). BYO capacity ceiling test ran but Pinata free tier limits were exhausted, so pin success baselines remain uncaptured.

repo: Playwright config's baseURL was hardcoded to localhost:5173 and did not respect BASE_URL env var — required explicit fix to support staging runs
Web3Auth SDK initialization on staging takes ~22.7s (vs fast local), causing 20s timeout failures in journey-timing.spec.ts
Cleanup helpers used hardcoded localhost:3000 API URL — needed to derive API URL from page context for staging compatibility
Vitest does not load .env files by default — must source them via shell before running or use explicit env forwarding
The staging throttle bypass (X-Throttle-Bypass header) works correctly end-to-end; failures were caused by running two load tests simultaneously against the same staging instance, not a code bug
Pinata free tier storage/pin limits can be exhausted quickly by load tests (50→1000 client escalation), invalidating BYO baseline results
BYO capacity ceiling test: all pin operations failed at 100% error rate due to Pinata plan limits being exceeded — not a provider code issue

code.finding: waitFor timeout of 20000ms too short for staging Web3Auth init (~22.7s); increased to accommodate staging cold start
deleteAccountViaPage helper derived API URL from hardcoded localhost — fixed to detect API URL from current page URL for staging compatibility
baseURL was hardcoded; fixed to read BASE_URL env var and skip local webServer when targeting external environments
Vitest does not auto-load .env files; env must be sourced via shell before test runner invocation
PinataProvider implementation is correct; pin failures in load tests were due to Pinata free tier quota exhaustion, not code issues

workflow: Running two load test suites simultaneously against the same staging instance saturates it regardless of throttle bypass — always run load tests sequentially against staging
Cherry-picking commits from worktree branches to the phase branch requires careful STATE.md conflict resolution — take the worktree version as it has the most current state
Git lock files from parallel agent worktrees need cleanup before spawning new agents against the same repo
BYO load testing requires a paid Pinata plan or a fresh account per test run to avoid quota exhaustion invalidating results
The classifyHandoffIfNeeded Claude Code runtime bug can cause agents to report 'failed' when they actually completed — always verify via SUMMARY.md and git commits

friction: Cherry-picking from multiple worktree branches caused repeated STATE.md merge conflicts requiring manual resolution
Git index locks from parallel worktrees blocked subsequent agent spawning — required manual cleanup
BASE_URL env var not respected by Playwright config caused the first staging test run to silently test localhost instead of staging
Vitest's lack of .env auto-loading caused the first two load test runs to skip all BYO tests silently with 'BYO_IPFS_ENDPOINT not set'
Running two load tests simultaneously caused both to fail with 429s, incorrectly suggesting a throttle bypass bug that required significant debugging time
Pinata free tier quota exhausted during BYO capacity ceiling escalation (50→1000 clients), invalidating all BYO pin baseline data
SSH access to staging Docker containers for env var inspection failed (timeout/key issue), blocking direct diagnosis
Phase was prematurely marked complete in ROADMAP.md before load test baselines were meaningful, requiring manual revert
open_items: BYO pin baselines (successful Pinata pins) uncaptured — requires paid Pinata plan or fresh free account with sufficient quota
Staging throttle bypass header not forwarded during createTestAccount in SDK test harness — confirmed working via bypass but needs documentation in harness comments
Browser load test (5 Chromium clients) hit 10-minute timeout — C4/C5 clients showed context exhaustion under contention; not investigated
Human verification item: new media test specs (streaming-playback, media-preview) need live environment run to confirm binary stub fixtures trigger expected AES-CTR/GCM code paths
Sustained load test threshold values need tuning for 200-client runs — current thresholds trigger false failure at p95 latencies that are actually acceptable at this scale
Learnings file created at .learnings/2026-03-29-staging-load-test-throttle-bypass.md documenting root cause of load test failures
